title: いつも～ — “always / usually”
summary: An adverb for something that happens nearly every time, or as a habit. In affirmative sentences it describes regular behavior.

patterns.gloss: いつも + verb (いつも六時に起きます)

body.p: Use it to talk about habits (いつもお茶を飲みます). It goes before the verb.
いつも〜ない means “not always”, so it happens sometimes. It is not the same as “never.”
よく means often and ときどき means sometimes. いつも is the highest frequency.

examples.ja: 私（わたし）はいつも六時（ろくじ）に起（お）きます。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa itsumo rokuji ni okimasu.
examples.tr: I always get up at six.

examples.ja: 母（はは）はいつも朝（あさ）ご飯（はん）を作（つく）ります。
examples.romaji: Haha wa itsumo asagohan o tsukurimasu.

examples.ja: 私（わたし）はいつもお茶（ちゃ）を飲（の）みます。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa itsumo ocha o nomimasu.

pitfalls: いつも〜ません does not mean “never.” For that use 全然 or 一度も.
Do not confuse it with いつ (when).
